channel.title: Parallax
channel.description: Same event, different vantage points. Geopolitical news compared across Western, Eastern, Middle Eastern and Russian outlets.

item.title: Donald Trump states that the conflict with Iran will end after the midterm elections.
item.description: President Donald Trump stated on September 10, 2026, that the conflict with Iran would conclude immediately following the American midterm elections. Western outlets reported the statement as a direct, standalone fact regarding the administration's current stance. In contrast, Middle Eastern and Russian sources framed the timeline as a response to Iranian nuclear ambitions and tactical maneuvers. These regional reports differ by focusing on the raw declaration versus the underlying geopolitical motivations behind the President's words.

item.title: Brent crude oil prices surpass 100 dollars per barrel amid escalating Middle East tensions.
item.description: On September 9, 2026, Brent crude oil prices surpassed $100 per barrel following retaliatory strikes between the United States and Iran. While all sources report the price hike, coverage differs significantly regarding the primary consequences of the surge. Western outlets focus on macroeconomic impacts like inflation and stock market volatility, whereas Eastern reports emphasize regional economic stability and specific logistical threats to Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz shipping routes.

item.title: The IAEA refers Iran to the UN Security Council over nuclear non-compliance issues.
item.description: On September 9, 2026, the IAEA Board of Governors voted 23-3-8 to refer Iran to the UN Security Council for nuclear non-compliance. Western outlets frame the move as a necessary enforcement of international law due to Tehran's lack of transparency. Conversely, Middle Eastern sources frame the decision as a politically motivated maneuver by Western powers, highlighting Iran's claims that the resolution is a reaction to regional military pressures.
